chart.programText:
def weighted_duration(base, product, filter_, groupby):
    durations     = data(base + '.time.ns.p75', filter=filter_ and filter('sf_product', product),  rollup='average').mean(by=groupby)

    counts     = data(base + '.count', filter=filter_ and filter('sf_product', product),  rollup='sum').sum(by=groupby)

    weight     = (durations * counts).sum(over='1m')


    return (weight / (counts.sum(over='1m') * 1000000000))

filter_ = filter('sf_environment', '*') and filter('app', '*') and filter('app.version','*')
groupby = ['app', 'sf_environment', 'os.name']
weighted_duration('rum.resource_request', 'mobile', filter_, groupby).publish(label='HTTP Latency in seconds from Mobile')

options.markdown:
Users expect apps to be responsive and fast to load. An app with a slow start time doesn’t meet this expectation, and can be disappointing to users. This sort of poor experience may cause a user to rate your app poorly on the Play store, or even abandon your app altogether.

[Vitals benchmarks](https://developer.android.com/topic/performance/vitals/launch-time) published by Google consider >5 seconds for cold starts and >1.5 seconds for hot starts excessive.
